name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STATEMENT_Q01 - Organization and functional divisions of neural system

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements regarding the organization of the human neural system:

Statement I: The central neural system (CNS) comprises the brain and spinal cord and is the primary site of information processing and control.

Statement II: Afferent nerve fibres transmit sensory impulses from peripheral tissues and organs to the central neural system.

Statement III: Efferent nerve fibres transmit regulatory impulses from the central neural system to peripheral effector tissues and organs.

Statement IV: The somatic neural system relays involuntary regulatory impulses from the central neural system to smooth muscles and internal viscera.

Statement V: The visceral nervous system is a component of the peripheral nervous system comprising nerves, fibres, ganglia, and plexuses connecting the central neural system with the viscera.

Choose the correct option from the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The human neural system is structurally organized into the central neural system (CNS) and the peripheral neural system (PNS). The PNS is functionally separated into sensory afferent pathways, motor efferent pathways, the voluntary somatic division, and the involuntary autonomic/visceral divisions.

Step 2: Evaluation of the claim concerning the central neural system
The brain and spinal cord together constitute the central neural system, which serves as the central command post for integrating, processing, and generating neural responses. Hence, this anatomical definition is factually accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the claim concerning afferent nerve fibres
Afferent nerve fibres convey incoming sensory information centripetally from receptors in tissues and bodily organs inward to the central neural system. Hence, this directional role is factually accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the claim concerning efferent nerve fibres
Efferent nerve fibres convey motor and regulatory signals centrifugally away from the central neural system outward to peripheral target organs and effectors. Hence, this physiological role is factually accurate.

Step 5: Evaluation of the claim concerning the somatic neural system
The somatic neural system is dedicated to voluntary control, relaying impulses from the central neural system specifically to skeletal muscles; involuntary conduction to smooth muscles and internal organs is governed by the autonomic neural system. Hence, attributing involuntary smooth muscle regulation to the somatic system is incorrect.

Step 6: Evaluation of the claim concerning the visceral nervous system
The visceral nervous system is an integral part of the peripheral neural system comprising the complete complex of nerves, fibres, ganglia, and plexuses that channel reciprocal impulse traffic between the central neural system and the viscera. Hence, this structural description is factually accurate.

Step 7: Final Conclusion
Among the evaluated assertions, the statements describing the central neural system, afferent fibres, efferent fibres, and the visceral nervous system are correct, whereas the statement misattributing smooth muscle control to the somatic neural system is incorrect.

answer.text: Statements I, II, III, and V are correct, while Statement IV is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STATEMENT_Q02 - Morphology and structural types of human neurons

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements regarding the structure and morphological types of neurons:

Statement I: The cell body and dendrites of a neuron contain granular bodies known as Nissl's granules.

Statement II: Dendrites are short, repeatedly branching processes that conduct nerve impulses away from the cell body toward target cells.

Statement III: The axon terminal arborizes into branches that end in bulb-like synaptic knobs containing neurotransmitter-filled vesicles.

Statement IV: Multipolar neurons have one axon and two or more dendrites and are characteristically located in the cerebral cortex.

Statement V: Unipolar neurons possess a cell body with only one axon and are typically found during the embryonic stage.

Choose the correct option from the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Neurons are the structural and functional units of the nervous system, characterized by a polarized architecture with receptive soma and dendrites, a conducting axon, and secretory terminal knobs, displaying morphological variation based on the number of emerging processes.

Step 2: Evaluation of the claim concerning Nissl's granules
Nissl's granules consist of rough endoplasmic reticulum and free ribosomes specialized for protein synthesis and are localized exclusively within the cell body and dendrites, being absent from the axon. Hence, this histological distribution is factually accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the claim concerning dendrite conduction direction
Dendrites are receptive processes that convey electrical impulses inward toward the cell body, whereas the axon conducts impulses away from the cell body. Hence, asserting that dendrites conduct impulses away from the cell body is incorrect.

Step 4: Evaluation of the claim concerning synaptic knobs
The distal extremity of an axon branches into terminal arborizations, each capping in a bulbous synaptic knob packed with membrane-bound synaptic vesicles that house neurotransmitter molecules. Hence, this morphological feature is factually accurate.

Step 5: Evaluation of the claim concerning multipolar neurons
Neurons featuring a single long axon and multiple branching dendrites represent multipolar neurons, which predominate numerically within the cerebral cortex. Hence, this anatomical localization is factually accurate.

Step 6: Evaluation of the claim concerning unipolar neurons
Unipolar neurons consist of a soma giving rise to only a single emerging axon without dendrites, a structural arrangement typical of early embryonic stages. Hence, this developmental classification is factually accurate.

Step 7: Final Conclusion
Among the evaluated assertions, the statements concerning Nissl's granules, synaptic knobs, multipolar neurons, and unipolar neurons are correct, whereas the statement mischaracterizing the conduction direction of dendrites is incorrect.

answer.text: Statements I, II, III, and IV are correct, while Statement V is incorrect.
Statements I, III, IV, and V are correct, while Statement II is incorrect.
Statements II, III, IV, and V are correct, while Statement I is incorrect.
Statements I, II, III, IV, and V are all correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STATEMENT_Q03 - Electrochemical basis of axonal resting membrane potential

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements regarding the resting membrane potential of an axon:

Statement I: In an unexcited, resting neuron, the axonal membrane is comparatively more permeable to potassium ions \(\left(\text{K}^{+}\right)\) than to sodium ions \(\left(\text{Na}^{+}\right)\).

Statement II: The resting axonal membrane is nearly impermeable to negatively charged intracellular proteins present in the axoplasm.

Statement III: In the resting state, the axoplasm contains a high concentration of \(\text{Na}^{+}\) and a low concentration of \(\text{K}^{+}\) relative to the extracellular fluid.

Statement IV: The sodium-potassium pump actively transports 3 sodium ions \(\left(\text{Na}^{+}\right)\) outward for every 2 potassium ions \(\left(\text{K}^{+}\right)\) into the cell.

Statement V: In a polarized resting state, the outer surface of the axonal membrane possesses a positive charge while its inner surface is negatively charged.

Choose the correct option from the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The resting membrane potential of excitable neurons is an electrically polarized steady state governed by differential resting ion channel permeabilities, impermeant intracellular macromolecular anions, and active primary ion transport.

Step 2: Evaluation of the claim concerning resting selective permeability
In the unexcited resting state, open potassium leak channels grant the axolemma significantly greater permeability to potassium ions compared to its negligible permeability to sodium ions. Hence, this permeability relationship is factually accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the claim concerning axoplasmic proteins
Large cellular proteins carrying negative charges remain confined within the axoplasm because the resting plasma membrane is completely impermeable to them. Hence, this impermeability characteristic is factually accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the claim concerning steady-state ionic concentrations
Due to selective permeability and active pumping, the axoplasm contains a high concentration of potassium ions and a low concentration of sodium ions, whereas the extracellular fluid has high sodium and low potassium. Hence, asserting that axoplasm has high sodium and low potassium is incorrect.

Step 5: Evaluation of the claim concerning the sodium-potassium pump
The ATP-dependent sodium-potassium pump maintains the ionic concentration gradients by actively expelling 3 sodium ions into the interstitial fluid while importing 2 potassium ions into the cell. Hence, this transport stoichiometry is factually accurate.

Step 6: Evaluation of the claim concerning resting membrane polarity
The net outward displacement of positive ions alongside trapped internal anions renders the exterior surface of the resting axonal membrane positively charged and its interior face negatively charged, establishing resting polarization. Hence, this electrical orientation is factually accurate.

Step 7: Final Conclusion
Among the evaluated assertions, the statements detailing selective permeability, protein impermeability, pump stoichiometry, and surface charge polarity are correct, whereas the statement inverting the intracellular sodium and potassium concentration gradients is incorrect.

answer.text: Statements I, II, and III are correct, while Statements IV and V are incorrect.
Statements I, III, IV, and V are correct, while Statement II is incorrect.
Statements I, II, IV, and V are correct, while Statement III is incorrect.
Statements I, II, III, IV, and V are all correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STATEMENT_Q04 - Electrophysiological mechanisms of nerve impulse propagation

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements regarding the generation and conduction of an action potential along an axon:

Statement I: Application of a stimulus at a site on the polarized membrane makes it freely permeable to \(\text{Na}^{+}\), causing a rapid influx of sodium ions.

Statement II: Rapid \(\text{Na}^{+}\) influx causes reversal of membrane polarity, making the outer surface negatively charged and the inner surface positively charged.

Statement III: The electrical potential difference across the plasma membrane at the excited site is termed the action potential or nerve impulse.

Statement IV: At adjacent resting sites ahead, current flows on the inner axonal surface from the excited site to the adjacent site, and on the outer surface from the adjacent site to the excited site.

Statement V: The rise in stimulus-induced permeability to \(\text{Na}^{+}\) is extremely short-lived and is rapidly followed by outward diffusion of \(\text{K}^{+}\), which restores the resting potential.

Choose the correct option from the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Nerve impulse conduction is an all-or-none electrophysiological event involving transient localized depolarization driven by voltage-gated sodium influx, self-propagating local electrical circuit loops, and rapid repolarization driven by potassium efflux.

Step 2: Evaluation of the claim concerning stimulus-induced sodium influx
Stimulation above threshold alters the configuration of voltage-gated sodium channels, rendering the membrane freely permeable to sodium ions, which rush into the axoplasm down their electrochemical gradient. Hence, this initial influx event is factually accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the claim concerning reversal of membrane polarity
The massive entry of positively charged sodium ions cancels the resting internal negativity and reverses the transmembrane polarity, turning the outer membrane surface negative and the internal face positive (depolarization). Hence, this polarity reversal is factually accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the claim concerning the action potential definition
The peak transmembrane electrical potential difference generated across the excited plasma membrane during this transient polarity reversal represents the action potential, physiologically defined as the nerve impulse. Hence, this definition is factually accurate.

Step 5: Evaluation of the claim concerning local current flow circuits
Because the excited site is internally positive while the adjacent unexcited segment is internally negative, local current flows internally from the excited site to the adjacent site, and externally returns in the opposite direction, depolarizing the adjacent zone. Hence, this circuit mechanism is factually accurate.

Step 6: Evaluation of the claim concerning repolarization via potassium efflux
Sodium channel activation is brief and is promptly succeeded by channel inactivation and opening of potassium channels; outward diffusion of potassium ions swiftly restores the resting electronegativity of the axoplasm. Hence, this repolarization sequence is factually accurate.

Step 7: Final Conclusion
All five evaluated assertions accurately depict the sequential biophysical and electrical events characterizing the generation, local circuit propagation, and repolarization of an axonal action potential.

answer.text: Statements I, II, and III are correct, while Statements IV and V are incorrect.
Statements I, III, IV, and V are correct, while Statement II is incorrect.
Statements II, III, IV, and V are correct, while Statement I is incorrect.
Statements I, II, III, IV, and V are all correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STATEMENT_Q05 - Junctional transmission across electrical chemical synapses

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements regarding the transmission of nerve impulses across synapses:

Statement I: At electrical synapses, pre-synaptic and post-synaptic membranes are separated by a wide fluid-filled gap termed the synaptic cleft.

Statement II: Transmission of an impulse across an electrical synapse is always faster than across a chemical synapse.

Statement III: Electrical synapses are rare in the human neural system compared to chemical synapses.

Statement IV: At chemical synapses, arrival of an action potential at the axon terminal stimulates synaptic vesicles to fuse with the pre-synaptic membrane and release neurotransmitters.

Statement V: Binding of released neurotransmitters to specific receptors on the post-synaptic membrane opens ion channels, which can generate either an excitatory or an inhibitory potential.

Choose the correct option from the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Synapses are specialized communicative junctions between adjacent neurons that operate either electrotonically through low-resistance gap channels (electrical synapses) or via quantal neurochemical exocytosis across a synaptic cleft (chemical synapses).

Step 2: Evaluation of the claim concerning the structural cleft at electrical synapses
At electrical synapses, the pre- and post-synaptic membranes reside in extremely intimate proximity without a prominent fluid-filled synaptic cleft, permitting direct uninterrupted ionic current flow; a wide, fluid-filled synaptic cleft is a definitive hallmark of chemical synapses. Hence, this structural claim is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of the claim concerning conduction velocity at electrical synapses
Because current crosses directly between communicating neurons without the delays inherent to biochemical vesicle exocytosis, cleft diffusion, and receptor activation, transmission across electrical synapses is consistently faster than across chemical synapses. Hence, this velocity comparison is factually accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the claim concerning the relative frequency of electrical synapses
Within human and higher mammalian nervous systems, electrical synapses occur infrequently, whereas chemical synapses constitute the predominant form of junctional transmission. Hence, this anatomical prevalence assertion is factually accurate.

Step 5: Evaluation of the claim concerning neurotransmitter release at chemical synapses
Depolarization of the axon terminal by an arriving action potential stimulates vesicular translocation and fusion with the pre-synaptic plasma membrane, discharging neurotransmitter molecules into the synaptic cleft. Hence, this exocytotic mechanism is factually accurate.

Step 6: Evaluation of the claim concerning post-synaptic receptor gating and potentials
Transmitter molecules diffuse across the cleft and bind to ligand-specific receptor complexes on the post-synaptic membrane, opening ion channels whose ion movements establish either depolarizing excitatory or hyperpolarizing inhibitory post-synaptic potentials. Hence, this signaling mechanism is factually accurate.

Step 7: Final Conclusion
Among the evaluated assertions, the statements describing synaptic speed, rarity of electrical synapses, vesicle exocytosis, and post-synaptic ion channel activation are correct, whereas the statement attributing a wide fluid-filled cleft to electrical synapses is incorrect.

answer.text: Statements II, III, IV, and V are correct, while Statement I is incorrect.
Statements I, II, III, and IV are correct, while Statement V is incorrect.
Statements I, III, IV, and V are correct, while Statement II is incorrect.
Statements I, II, III, IV, and V are all correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STATEMENT_Q06 - Structural and functional anatomy of human brain

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements regarding the structure and functional divisions of the human brain:

Statement I: The cranial meninges comprise an outer dura mater, a thin middle arachnoid, and an inner pia mater that contacts the brain tissue.

Statement II: The left and right cerebral hemispheres are interconnected by a massive nerve tract called the corpus callosum.

Statement III: The association areas of the cerebral cortex are purely motor in function and directly execute voluntary skeletal muscle contractions.

Statement IV: The hypothalamus contains centres controlling body temperature, urge for eating and drinking, and secretes hypothalamic hormones.

Statement V: The brain stem connects the brain and spinal cord and is constituted by the midbrain, pons, and medulla oblongata.

Choose the correct option from the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The human brain is protected by the skull and three meningeal coverings, divided into forebrain, midbrain, and hindbrain, with specialized structures mediating sensory integration, executive cognition, neuroendocrine control, and vital autonomic reflexes.

Step 2: Evaluation of the claim concerning the cranial meninges
The brain is encapsulated by three distinct protective meningeal layers: the outer tough dura mater, the intermediate delicate arachnoid mater, and the innermost vascular pia mater in direct histological contact with brain parenchyma. Hence, this anatomical layering is factually accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the claim concerning the corpus callosum
The cerebral hemispheres are longitudinally separated by a deep fissure but structurally connected along their base by a broad transverse commissural tract of myelinated nerve fibres termed the corpus callosum. Hence, this anatomical connection is factually accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the claim concerning cerebral association areas
Cortical association areas are neither clearly sensory nor purely motor; instead, they integrate multi-modal information to mediate complex associative faculties including memory, communication, and intersensory synthesis. Hence, asserting that association areas are purely motor execution areas is incorrect.

Step 5: Evaluation of the claim concerning the hypothalamus
Located at the base of the thalamus, the hypothalamus contains discrete regulatory nuclei controlling thermoregulation, hunger, and thirst, as well as neurosecretory perikarya synthesizing regulatory hypothalamic hormones. Hence, this physiological description is factually accurate.

Step 6: Evaluation of the claim concerning the brain stem
The brain stem acts as the structural and communicative bridge linking the higher cerebral centers to the spinal cord, and it is anatomically composed of three regions: the midbrain, the pons, and the medulla oblongata. Hence, this structural definition is factually accurate.

Step 7: Final Conclusion
Among the evaluated assertions, the statements describing the cranial meninges, corpus callosum, hypothalamus, and brain stem are correct, whereas the statement misclassifying association areas as purely motor is incorrect.

answer.text: Statements I, II, III, and IV are correct, while Statement V is incorrect.
Statements I, II, IV, and V are correct, while Statement III is incorrect.
